Perhaps in the department of etching no artist has so happily translated the pictures of Claude de Lorraine as Francis Vivares; that is, with respect to aerial perspective, the peculiar characteristic of Claude. But his merits are not confined to this master alone; for he followed Ruydaile, Bergheim, Gaintborough, and Cuype, with great success. He has such a free delivery of style, that almost every one who examines his works is irretrievably impressed with an idea of performing the very fame.
